knownProductionState.lastKnownIssue: both public hosts serve the same successful but stale deployment: source commit 49575ba is nine commits behind current main. Three article first-response aborts were logged between 12:57Z and 13:16Z. The handler's five-second timer explains the abort message; the individual fetch delay and reader impact are not correlated in available logs.
knownProductionState.note: Read-only GET / and /api/healthz requests at 12:49:04Z and repeat safe probes around 13:12Z returned HTTP 200 on both public hosts with identical stale fingerprints. Replit metadata reports a public active successful Autoscale deployment; the available metadata and deployment-log callback did not expose a deployment ID or startup build record. Log searches found article first-response aborts at 12:57:11.635Z, 13:07:33.515Z, and 13:15:57.320Z; no further match appeared after 13:16:53Z in the latest query. The renderer starts a five-second timer for the API fetch plus JSON parsing; the server catches timeout errors into its 503/noindex fallback, but logs omit route, status, elapsed time, and a cross-service request ID. Nearby newsroom-content requests return 200, but are not provably the same calls. Current workspace HEAD at the investigation check is edaa5172a238d9e6e061c4de0502318b531e127f, nine commits ahead of production; the last locally verified build and API health headers are from 99710e4e3363aeb072a0dbf2cdae144c51cc3253. Changes after that build are documentation-only, and the source-content/artifact hashes are unchanged. The article-render handler is unchanged from production, so publishing alone will not change this timeout path. No production editorial writes, publishing automation, or deployment occurred. Publishing is on hold at the user's request.
